variant.description:
HitSpark replaces Final Fantasy XIV's combat text with its own renderer: better fonts, tuned motion and real impact on critical hits.

WHAT YOU GET

- Every kind of combat text redrawn: damage dealt and taken, healing, misses and evades, status effects, experience, crafting and loot.
- Eight built-in presets, each a complete look: Classic+, Heroic, Tally, Onslaught, Elemental, Grim, Minimal and Retro.
- Real motion: arcs, fountains, rising and falling paths, scrolling columns, and punch, shake, flash, sparks and trails on crits.
- Multi-hits and damage over time that roll up into one number, with DoT ticks in their own colour.
- Other players' numbers shown smaller, or hidden, for your party and for everyone else.
- A style editor for every category with a live preview, and presets you can share as a short code.

GETTING STARTED

Type /hitspark (or /hs) to open the settings and pick a preset. /hitspark test plays sample numbers on you and your target, even out of combat.
Found a bug or have an idea? Settings > Diagnostics copies a report and opens a GitHub issue for you.

PLAYS BY THE RULES

HitSpark is purely cosmetic: it only redraws text the game already shows you and follows the game's own flying text and pop-up text options. If a game update breaks it, the game's own numbers come back on their own. Settings and presets are stored locally and nothing is ever sent anywhere.

variant.author: GitHixy
variant.changelog:
- Positionals: on Monk, Dragoon, Ninja, Samurai, Reaper and Viper, a small "Rear" or "Flank" now shows above your damage when you land a positional, and "Rear missed" or "Flank missed" when you don't. They have their own styles in every preset, so you can restyle or hide them.
- New "Below game UI" option: numbers slide under your hotbars, party list, chat and the other game windows instead of covering them, while your target's bars and your own HP/MP stay on top. Off by default.
- New "Max distance" option: numbers from other people more than 50 yalms away, like a FATE across the map, are no longer shown. You can change the distance or turn the limit off.
- Fixed numbers (DoT ticks above all) showing during cutscenes in the middle of a duty.
variant.description:
HitSpark replaces Final Fantasy XIV's combat text with its own renderer: better fonts, tuned motion and real impact on critical hits.

WHAT YOU GET

- Every kind of combat text redrawn: damage dealt and taken, healing, misses and evades, status effects, experience, crafting and loot.
- Eight built-in presets, each a complete look: Classic+, Heroic, Tally, Onslaught, Elemental, Grim, Minimal and Retro.
- Real motion: arcs, fountains, rising and falling paths, scrolling columns, and punch, shake, flash, sparks and trails on crits.
- Multi-hits and damage over time that roll up into one number, with DoT ticks in their own colour.
- Other players' numbers shown smaller, or hidden, for your party and for everyone else, with a distance limit.
- Rear and flank hints for positionals, and an option to let numbers pass under the game's UI.
- A style editor for every category with a live preview, and presets you can share as a short code.

GETTING STARTED

Type /hitspark (or /hs) to open the settings and pick a preset. /hitspark test plays sample numbers on you and your target, even out of combat.
Found a bug or have an idea? Settings > Diagnostics copies a report and opens a GitHub issue for you.

PLAYS BY THE RULES

HitSpark is purely cosmetic: it redraws text the game already shows you and follows the game's own flying text and pop-up text options. The only extra is the optional positional hint, worked out from where you're standing. If a game update breaks it, the game's own numbers come back on their own. Settings and presets are stored locally and nothing is ever sent anywhere.
